anchor.quote: The work of government has its basis in legislation. When you write about a particular policy, service or program, you often need to refer to recent changes to the relevant law (amending legislation). You will also name the legislation that currently applies (consolidated legislation). You might have to write about changes in the law over time. In this case, you would mention amending legislation that is no longer in force.

covers.quote: Cite legal material consistently and accurately
It’s important to cite legal sources in a consistent and accurate way across government.

rules.quote: Follow one style consistently to help people read and use the information.
rules.violation_condition: Comparable legal citations within the same content use inconsistent citation conventions.
when: Compare citations for which the chosen citation style prescribes the same conventions; differences required for different source types are not inconsistencies.
rules.why: G-4: capture the explicit consistency instruction once rather than adding overlapping checks from its broad summaries.

rules.violation_condition: A legislation citation gives an incorrect title for the legislation being cited.
when: Check the title against the authorised title of the legislation in the relevant jurisdiction.
rules.why: G-1: this heading states a distinct title-accuracy check, not merely a grouping; the database-search instructions are G-5 advice.

covers.quote: Unless it is obvious from the context:
Follow the title with the rest of the citation.
Always list the legislation or case name first in a basic note.
Explanatory notes might vary.

parts.quote: The Loans Security Act 1973 (subsection 5A(b)) provides for ...
Commonwealth legislation (Loans Security Act 1973,subsection 5A(b)) provides for ...
Commonwealth legislation (subsection 5A(b), Loans Security Act 1973) provides for ...

2 Section 48 of the Australian Constitution provides for the payment of members of parliament. Commonwealth Acts include Remuneration and Allowances Act 1990, Remuneration Tribunal Act 1973, Ministers of State Act 1952, ...other Acts and associated delegated legislation.

rules.quote: Put the title first when writing in-text citations, footnotes and endnotes.
rules.specification: The page does not define when context makes title-first order unnecessary or explicitly explain how that qualification interacts with the later instruction to always put the name first in a basic note.
rules.violation_condition: Citation details precede the legislation title, or a basic legal note begins with material other than the legislation or case name, outside the stated exceptions.
when: The general legislation instruction applies to in-text citations, footnotes and endnotes, unless it is obvious from the context.
For a basic note, the page says to always list the legislation or case name first.
Explanatory notes may vary.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: title/name-first order is one check across citation contexts; G-3: explanatory-note variation is an exception, not another rule.

covers.quote: Users find the note by matching the number.

parts.quote: The levy threshold is indexed quarterly.1
The legislative basis for parliamentary remuneration and entitlements is complex.2

2 Section 48 of the Australian Constitution provides for the payment of members of parliament. Commonwealth Acts include Remuneration and Allowances Act 1990, Remuneration Tribunal Act 1973, Ministers of State Act 1952, ...other Acts and associated delegated legislation.

rules.quote: Each note has the corresponding superscript reference marker before it.
rules.violation_condition: A note lacks its corresponding preceding superscript reference marker, including where its number does not match the reference number.
when: When footnotes or endnotes are used.
rules.why: G-2: the corresponding marker and matching number form one note-reference correspondence check.

rules.quote: Use hyperlinked endnotes in digital content.
rules.violation_condition: An endnote in digital content is not accessible through a hyperlink from its reference marker.
when: In digital content that uses endnotes.
rules.why: G-2: digital content limits the hyperlink check; this does not require every document to contain endnotes.

covers.quote: Certain government agencies and specialist legal publications will use a reference list.
People need the list to understand the content.
The content includes a reference list for non-legal sources.
It is agency style to have a reference list.

rules.quote: Most government writers should only include a reference list if one of these applies:
rules.specification: The page does not fully identify the writers outside ‘Most government writers’; it separately notes reference-list use by certain agencies and specialist legal publications.
rules.violation_condition: General government content includes a legal reference list even though readers do not need it to understand the content, there is no reference list for non-legal sources, and agency style does not call for one.
when: For the general government writing covered by ‘Most government writers’.
A reference list is permitted if people need it to understand the content.
A reference list is permitted if the content includes a reference list for non-legal sources.
A reference list is permitted if agency style requires one.
These conditions permit a reference list; they do not by themselves require one.
rules.why: G-2: the three alternatives govern one reference-list inclusion check; G-3: permission under those conditions is not a separate requirement.
